title: Convert an LLC to a C-Corp
summary: The LLC is about to raise or grant options, so it becomes a Delaware C-Corp: assess the timing and tax consequences, get counsel's sign-off, have the members approve a plan of conversion, file the Certificate of Conversion together with the Certificate of Incorporation, then re-issue equity and refile 83(b) elections under the new corporation.

parts.title: Assess whether and when to convert
parts.guidance: Compare the LLC’s current state, ownership, tax classification, assets and contracts with the proposed corporate structure and financing plans. Identify why conversion is useful now and what would change for each owner. Bring tax, legal and timing questions to the advisers before deciding on the transaction. Establish the available legal route and tax treatment for this transaction.

parts.title: Get tax and legal advice on the conversion
parts.guidance: Review the operating agreement, ownership ledger, returns, balance sheet, material contracts and planned financing with legal and tax advisers. Resolve the available conversion route, required approvals, ownership exchange, asset treatment, tax effects and filing sequence for the states involved. Identify questions that prevent document preparation or filing, and agree who will resolve them.

parts.title: Prepare the plan of conversion and C-Corp charter documents
parts.guidance: Draft the conversion plan, ownership exchange and corporate charter from the chosen transaction structure. Reconcile member interests, stock classes, authorized shares and outstanding rights so the documents describe the same economics. Flag missing consents, contract actions and closing conditions for counsel. The review package should show what becomes effective through filing and what requires a separate closing action.

parts.title: Members sign the plan of conversion and written consent
parts.guidance: Present the final conversion plan with the ownership changes, effective timing and remaining conditions. Confirm the approvals required by the LLC agreement and applicable law, then obtain them from the actual members or other holders. Check capacities, voting interests and document versions. Missing or qualified approvals must be resolved before the filer relies on the conversion as authorized.

parts.title: File the Certificate of Conversion and Certificate of Incorporation
parts.guidance: Follow the filing package and sequence confirmed for the transaction. For a Delaware corporate conversion, check the Certificate of Conversion and Certificate of Incorporation against DGCL section 265 and the approved plan. The authorized signer reviews names, fees and effective timing before submission. Track both filings through acceptance. Other jurisdictions or structures require their own confirmed package.

verify.how: The Delaware entity search shows the new corporation, with the conversion on its filing history.

cost.note: Minimum: $184 Certificate of Conversion (other entity to corporation) plus the $109 minimum Certificate of Incorporation that must be filed simultaneously — the incorporation part varies with authorized stock.

parts.title: Receive the stamped conversion and incorporation certificates
parts.guidance: Obtain the accepted conversion and incorporation records from the relevant registries. Compare entity identity, filing dates and effective times with the transaction plan and resolve discrepancies with counsel. Use those verified details for equity, bank and tax changes. Keep applications marked pending until acceptance is established, with the issued records available in the corporate archive.

parts.title: Adopt bylaws and issue founder stock under the C-Corp
parts.guidance: Prepare bylaws, initial corporate actions and stock records from the approved conversion plan. Reconcile each exchanged LLC interest and any new issuance to the post-conversion holdings. Obtain the required corporate approvals and verify consideration and closing conditions before recording issuance. The resulting stock ledger should trace each holding to its executed transaction documents.

parts.title: Founders sign the new stock purchase agreements
parts.guidance: Check each founder’s purchase or exchange agreement against the conversion plan and corporate approvals: class, share count, price or consideration, vesting, restrictions and interests replaced. Resolve conflicting terms before the parties sign. Keep executed agreements and consideration or transfer evidence together. Record the actual transaction date accurately for later tax review.

parts.title: Sign the 83(b) elections
parts.guidance: For a potentially relevant restricted-property transfer, give the founder’s tax adviser the transfer date, restrictions, value, amount paid and executed agreement. If the founder chooses an applicable section 83(b) election, prepare it from those facts and have the founder review and sign. Arrange filing promptly. The conversion itself does not establish an election need, and a signed election is still unfiled.

parts.title: File the 83(b) elections with the IRS
parts.guidance: For each founder making an applicable section 83(b) election, verify the property-transfer date, deadline and filing requirements with the tax adviser. Arrange the authorized submission under the current IRS instructions and obtain filing evidence. Keep the signed election and required company or transferee copies. Verify filing evidence for each founder who elected.

verify.how: Online submissions in the taxpayer's IRS Online Account confirm on submit — retain the confirmation. For the mail rail, retain the date-stamped copy and the USPS certified-mail receipt — the IRS sends no confirmation; your proof of mailing within the 30-day window is the record.

cost.note: No IRS filing fee for an 83(b) election — the cost is certified-mail postage.

parts.title: Update bank, payroll, and state registrations to the corporation
parts.guidance: Use the accepted conversion records and tax conclusions to identify changes needed at banks, payroll, insurers, contracting systems and state accounts. Determine whether each needs an amendment, new account or supporting document. Authorized account holders approve the updates and verify the resulting entity details. Keep old services available until payments, payroll and record access can continue through the transition.

geoNotes.summary: The analog is converting an LLP into a private limited company under Companies Act s.366 (form URC-1, plus fresh incorporation paperwork) — an MCA process fronted by NSWS since mca.gov.in blocks automated access; it is slow and tax-sensitive, so many simply incorporate fresh.

The analog move is incorporating an existing sole trade or partnership into a limited company; HMRC's Incorporation Relief defers the capital gains tax when the business transfers in exchange for shares.

Changing legal form is a statutory Formwechsel under the Umwandlungsgesetz (e.g. UG to GmbH, or GbR into GmbH) — notarized, registered in the Handelsregister, and usually tax-neutral if done under the UmwStG.

The classic pre-fundraise move is transforming a SARL into a SAS: an extraordinary shareholders' decision, a commissaire report, amended statuts, then the transformation filed through the guichet unique.

The move is a statutory transformação de sociedade under the Código das Sociedades Comerciais (e.g. Lda to SA ahead of institutional money) — shareholder-resolved, registered at the commercial registry, with the company's legal identity continuing.

With no LLC to convert, the analog is incorporating an existing unincorporated business: a section 85 rollover transfers the assets into a corporation in exchange for shares with the capital gain deferred by joint election.

metadata.supportReason: The go/no-go call and counsel review are human judgment, member and founder signatures are legally required acts, and Delaware's conversion filing is portal/mail work with no API — the system preps documents and tracks progress but cannot file.
